prompts: The game went down in June and we owe the team an incident report. The logs and their notes are in {WS}/logs. When did it start and end, how long was it, did we keep our monthly availability target, and why did it happen? Record it in {WS}/result.json: start, end, minutes_down, availability_june_pct, slo_999_ok, root_cause.
answers:
**Found:** One incident on 2026-06-02, 03:17:42 → 03:53:31 (35.82 min down). June availability 99.917% — above the 99.9% SLO, so `slo_999_ok: true`. Root cause: /data disk full — SaveGame writes failed with "No space left on device", the watchdog restart loop kept dying (exit 137) until backup rotation freed 38.2 GB at 03:52:10, then the server came back at 03:53:31.

**How I know it's right:**
- README defines the incident window: "Down = from the first save error to the 'server ready' line", SLO 99.9%, one incident, June = 30 days.
- Grep over all three logs found exactly two save errors (03:17:42, 03:18:00) and one "server ready" (03:53:31) — both in gameserver-2026-06-02.log; the only other ERROR in June (06-01 RCON auth failure) is not a save error, so the window is unique.
- Read the log lines 245–299: heartbeats normal until 03:17:26, then the save errors, FATAL watchdog restart, ~30 failed restarts, "backup rotation freed 38.2 GB on /data" at 03:52:10, "server ready" at 03:53:31, heartbeats resume.
- Arithmetic verified by script: (03:53:31 − 03:17:42) = 35.82 min; (1 − 35.82/43200) × 100 = 99.917%.

**Assumptions:** timestamps are UTC (logs carry no zone); "minutes_down" is the exact fractional duration (35.82), not rounded to whole minutes; availability = (total June minutes − down minutes) / total June minutes per the README's 30-day June.

`./result.json` written with all six fields. No browser tabs or windows were opened, so nothing to close.
